law005_admissibility_boundary_transition.name: Admissibility Boundary Transition Law
law005_admissibility_boundary_transition.purpose: Define explicit transition behavior near admissibility boundaries under projected transport updates.

candidate_law_statement.informal: Projected continuation approaching admissibility boundaries may stabilize, split, collapse, prune, or fail depending on admissibility margin, transport magnitude, and local topology constraints.
candidate_law_statement.boundary_transition_condition: If admissibility_margin_A(Π_{A_α}(T_α)) → 0, boundary-sensitive continuation modes may activate.
candidate_law_statement.projection_failure_condition: If Π_{A_α}(T_α) is undefined or leaves A_α, continuation may branch-collapse, prune, destabilize, or enter preserved failure states.
candidate_law_statement.branch_transition_condition: Boundary proximity may preserve multi-valued continuation through branch splitting or branch pruning rather than forced unique projection.
candidate_law_statement.important_note: This is a candidate admissibility-boundary transition law, not a proof of global stability, smooth boundary topology, or physical transition structure.
